How to do itAb Wheel Rollout

Back line

Right
STRAIGHT LINE
Wrong
BACK ARCHED

Right: Straight line from knees to head.

Wrong: Low back arched.

Knees to head in one line, back straight.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back archesThe low back arches as the arms reach overhead.
Roll out2 s
Roll back1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your belly and under your arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The whole trunk braces to keep the body straight.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansAn arching low back can result in injury.

    FixRoll out less far and slower.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Kneel on a soft pad, hands on the wheel, shoulder-width apart.

  2. 2

    Set the wheel on the floor just in front of your knees.

  3. 3

    Brace and squeeze your glutes. Start with your trunk, not your arms.

  4. 4

    New? Kneel, not standing, and roll toward a wall that stops you.

  5. 5

    Start short, roll further as strength grows. Pull back with your lats.

Risks and when to stop

  • An arching or rotating torso can result in injury.
  • Rolling out too fast can increase the risk of arching or rotating.
  • A fall in a standing rollout has caused serious spine injury.

How to do itBird Dog

Back line

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
LOW BACK ARCHES

Right: Back flat as the leg rises.

Wrong: Low back sagging into an arch.

Head

Right
EYES DOWN
Wrong
HEAD LIFTED

Right: Head in line, eyes on the floor.

Wrong: Head lifted to look forward.

Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back archesThe low back sags into an arch as the leg rises.
  2. Leg too highThe leg lifts too high, past parallel to the floor.
Reach3 s
Hold3 s
Return3 s
Look closer

Grip

Hands under the shoulders, fingers facing forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Back arching as leg rises

    Fix: Raise the limbs only as high as your low back holds.

  • Head lifted to look forward

    Fix: Keep your eyes on the floor, head in line with your spine.

  • Hips tilting or rotating

    Fix: Press down with your unmoving hand, knee and toes. Hips level.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your low back, glutes and belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching the back can lead to lower back pain.

    FixStop if any pain occurs. Keep your back flat.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Kneel on a mat, knees and feet hip-width apart.

  2. 2

    Put a cushion or folded towel under your knees.

  3. 3

    Hands on the mat under your shoulders, fingers forward.

  4. 4

    Knees under your hips. Keep hips and shoulders level.

  5. 5

    Hold your spine neutral, back flat. Move slowly and keep breathing.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching or rounding the back puts increased stress on the lumbar spine.
  • Lifting your head to look forward takes your neck out of alignment.

How to do itSide Plank

Hip line

Right
HIPS UP
Wrong
HIPS SINK

Right: Hips lifted in line with ribs and legs.

Wrong: Hips sinking toward the floor.

Bottom shoulder

Right
SHOULDER DOWN
Wrong

Right: Elbow under the shoulder, shoulder down.

Wrong: Shoulder shrugged up toward the ear.

Bottom elbow sits under the shoulder.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips sinkThe hips sink toward the floor.
Hold30–60 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the side of your waist, on the lower side.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The abs help as a secondary muscle.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe shoulder is shrugging up.

    FixPull your shoulder down and pad the elbow.

  • Usually meansToo much pressure on that joint.

    FixStop the exercise.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your side, elbow under your shoulder, forearm on a mat.

  2. 2

    Stack your top leg on your bottom leg.

  3. 3

    Press elbow and foot down. Lift hips in line, head to feet.

  4. 4

    Top hand on your hip. Hold as steadily as you can.

  5. 5

    Brace and keep breathing, slow and deep.

Risks and when to stop

  • Too much pressure inside the top knee or foot may stress those joints.
  • Sinking hips take work off your trunk. Lift them, or end the hold.
  • Holding your breath is one of the biggest side-plank mistakes.

Knee pain

Severe pain, badly swollen, changed shape, locking, giving way, or can't put weight on it? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your low back and glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansLifting your head too high strains your neck.

    FixKeep your eyes down and your neck neutral.

  • FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie face down on a mat, legs straight, toes pointing away.

  2. 2

    Arms overhead, palms facing each other, shoulders down and back.

  3. 3

    Relax your head in line. Arms and legs straight, no rotation.

  4. 4

    Tighten your abs to steady your spine. Keep breathing steadily.

  5. 5

    Squeeze your glutes and slowly lift arms and legs a few inches.

Risks and when to stop

  • Lifting your head too high can strain your neck.
  • Lifting too high can cause strain.
  • Jerky, uncontrolled movements raise your risk of injury.

How to do itCable Crunch

Hips still

Right
HIPS STILL
Wrong
HIPS MOVE

Right: Hips still and raised, the spine curling.

Wrong: Hips moving to pull, not only the spine.

Keep the hips still and raised while only the spine bends.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips moveThe hips move back to pull while the spine stays straight.
Crunch2 s
Hold1 s
Return3 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansMoving your hips puts tension on your hip flexors.

    FixKeep your hips still. Only your spine bends.

  • Usually meansReps not controlled, or chin not tucked.

    FixKeep the movement controlled and your chin tucked.

  • Usually meansRounding your lower back.

    FixStop at elbows near thighs, without rounding your lower back excessively.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Fix a rope to the high pulley. Choose a light-to-moderate weight.

  2. 2

    Kneel a few feet from the machine, facing it, stance about hip-to-shoulder-width.

  3. 3

    Hold rope ends either side of your head. Yanking? Arms only hold.

  4. 4

    Hinge back slightly from your hips to raise them. Tuck your chin.

  5. 5

    Brace, breathe out and curl. Breathe in, straighten slowly, abs tense.

Risks and when to stop

  • Keep the movement controlled to avoid neck strain.
  • Acute lower back pain? Avoid this exercise.
  • Too much weight risks overloading your traps, arms and back instead of your abs.

How to do itHollow Body Hold

Leg height

Right
LEGS LIFTED
Wrong
LEGS TOO LOW

Right: Legs straight, about 15 to 30 degrees off the floor.

Wrong: Legs not lifted high enough.

Low back

Right
BACK DOWN
Wrong
BACK ARCHES

Right: Lower back flat on the floor, no space under it.

Wrong: Lower back arched off the floor.

Press your low back flat to the floor the whole hold.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Legs too lowYour legs sink too low, so the hip flexors take over.
Holdmax 30 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour hip flexors are working overtime.

    FixLift your legs off the floor, but no higher than about 30 degrees.

  • Usually meansYour lower back is lifting off the floor.

    FixStop the set, or use an easier version.

  • Usually meansYour neck is hyperextending.

    FixLower your chin and look down at your feet, without tucking it.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your back, legs straight, feet together.

  2. 2

    Reach your arms overhead, biceps by your ears.

  3. 3

    Breathe out, pull your ribs down, press your lower back flat.

  4. 4

    Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor and hold.

  5. 5

    Body in a crescent, hips down. Breathe shallowly, don't hold your breath.

Risks and when to stop

  • An arched lower back could lead to injury.
  • Dropping shoulder blades and head may cause low back pain. Lower your limbs, rest.
  • Hyperextending your neck could result in neck pain.

How to do itReverse Crunch

Knee angle

Right
KNEES AT 90
Wrong
KNEES TUCK

Right: Knees bent at 90 degrees.

Wrong: Knees tucked too far toward the chest.

Hip curl

Right
HIPS CURL UP
Wrong

Right: Hips and lower back curled off the floor.

Keep the knee angle at 90 degrees the whole rep.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Knees tuckThe knees tuck in toward your chest and the knee angle closes.
Curl2 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your belly, maybe more in your lower abs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansSome hip flexor work is normal.

    FixStart each rep with your abs, not your legs.

  • Usually meansKnees tucked too far, weight rolling toward your neck.

    FixKeep your knees at 90 degrees. Stop if sharp pain occurs.

  • Usually meansYour lower back arching can strain it.

    FixBrace so it doesn't arch. Stop if sharp pain occurs.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your back, arms by your sides, palms down.

  2. 2

    Brace, lift your feet, knees over hips and bent to 90 degrees.

  3. 3

    Lower back flat. Hard to flatten? Put your hands under your hips.

  4. 4

    Breathe out, curl your hips toward your ribs, tailbone off the floor.

  5. 5

    Hold briefly. Breathe in and roll down slowly, vertebra by vertebra.

Risks and when to stop

  • Tucking your knees too far brings your weight onto your upper back and neck.
  • If your lower back arches, it can strain your lower back.
  • Lowering? Keep your knees over your hips, not past, to spare your low back.

Tells

LowerSlow

Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your belly and sides of your waist.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour back is arching off the mat.

    FixFinish the rep you're on and rest.

  • Usually meansLooking down at your legs strains your neck.

    FixLook straight up at the ceiling.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your back on a mat.

  2. 2

    Knees at 90 degrees over your hips, arms straight above your chest.

  3. 3

    Brace, press your lower back into the mat, shoulders down and back.

  4. 4

    Breathe in and slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg.

  5. 5

    Touch hand and heel lightly, without resting. Breathe out, return, switch sides.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching your back could contribute to a back injury.
  • Looking down at your legs strains your neck.
  • Holding your breath during the reps is a mistake.

Low back

Right
BACK DOWN
Wrong

Right: Lower back flat on the floor, braced.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Low back archesYour low back arches off the floor at the start of the rep.
Lower 
Lift 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansAn arched lower back lets your hip flexors take over.

    FixKeep your lower back flat on the floor.

  • Usually meansArching your back could bring discomfort or pain here.

    FixBrace, and keep your lower back touching the floor.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie on your back, legs straight, toes gently pressed together.

  2. 2

    Extend your arms above your head.

  3. 3

    Breathe in, tense your middle, push your pelvis and lower back down.

  4. 4

    Lift legs and torso together, upper body leading, reaching toward your toes.

  5. 5

    Legs straight as you can. Return with heels just off the floor.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching your back could bring serious discomfort or pain in your lower back.
  • Control your speed and watch your low back to reduce the chance of injury.
  • Legs flopping around cost you balance. Legs starting the lift is a mistake.
